title: Impersonal se: how a word is usually defined

sections.content: You know impersonal *se* from B1 Unit 6: *se* + a third-person verb says what is said or done in general, without naming anyone (*Se habla español aquí*). You also know *soler* from B1 Unit 5. Together they give *se suele* + infinitive: "it is usually …". Historians use it to report how a disputed word is normally used, because populism has no single definition.

items.spanish: Se suele llamar populismo a los movimientos que hablaban en nombre del pueblo.
items.english: The movements that spoke in the name of the people are usually called populism.

items.spanish: Se suele hablar de una relación directa entre el líder y sus seguidores.
items.english: People usually speak of a direct relationship between the leader and his followers.

items.spanish: Se dice que el líder hablaba directamente a la gente.
items.english: It is said that the leader spoke directly to the people.

items.spanish: No se suele llegar a un acuerdo sobre la definición de populismo.
items.english: People do not usually reach an agreement on the definition of populism.

sections.content: Keep the verb singular when *se* is impersonal and the object comes with *a*: *se suele llamar populismo a los movimientos*. To say who holds the view, add *según*: *según algunos historiadores, se suele …*.
